title: Public IP addresses
learningObjective: Create and configure public IP addresses and prefixes, choosing SKU, assignment, tier and zone settings, and associate them with resources.
foundation: A public IP address lets internet clients reach an Azure resource (or lets it be identified on the internet).
You can attach public IPs to VM NICs, load balancers, application gateways, VPN gateways, NAT gateways, Azure Firewall and Bastion.
engineer: SKU: Standard is the only SKU for new deployments (Basic public IPs were retired on 30 September 2025). Standard IPs use static assignment, are secure by default (closed to inbound until an NSG allows traffic) and support availability zones.
Zones: zone-redundant (survives zone failure), zonal (pinned to one zone) or no zone. The zone setting can't be changed after creation.
Tier: Regional or Global (Global is used with the cross-region load balancer). Routing preference: Microsoft network (default) or Internet (cheaper, uses ISP networks).
Public IP prefixes reserve a contiguous range (for example /28) of static addresses for allow-listing. IP addresses are billed per hour, whether or not they're associated.
Associate or dissociate a public IP on a NIC's IP configuration. A VM can have a public IP per IP configuration; for outbound-only internet access prefer a NAT gateway.

example.title: A partner allow-list
body: A partner must allow-list Contoso's outbound addresses. Contoso creates a /30 public IP prefix and assigns its addresses to a NAT gateway, so all outbound traffic uses four known IPs.

prerequisites: An Azure subscription and a resource group (rg-net)
permissions: Network Contributor on the resource group
limits: Public IP quota per region (default varies by subscription)
Zone and SKU cannot be changed after creation
portal: Create a resource > Public IP address: choose SKU Standard, tier Regional, zone-redundant, IP version IPv4.
VM > Networking > NIC > IP configurations > ipconfig1 > associate the public IP.
Public IP prefixes > Create to reserve a range.
configuration.cli:
az network public-ip create -g rg-net -n pip-web --sku Standard --allocation-method Static --zone 1 2 3
az network nic ip-config update -g rg-net --nic-name vm-web-nic -n ipconfig1 --public-ip-address pip-web
az network public-ip prefix create -g rg-net -n ippre-out --length 30
configuration.powershell:
New-AzPublicIpAddress -ResourceGroupName rg-net -Name pip-web -Location eastus -Sku Standard -AllocationMethod Static -Zone 1,2,3
$nic = Get-AzNetworkInterface -Name vm-web-nic -ResourceGroupName rg-net
$nic.IpConfigurations[0].PublicIpAddress = Get-AzPublicIpAddress -Name pip-web -ResourceGroupName rg-net
$nic | Set-AzNetworkInterface

lab.objective: Configure a Standard public IP correctly.
steps: Apply 'Standard without NSG' and read why inbound fails.
expected: Standard is static and secure by default

validation.text: Configured a reachable Standard public IP

failureScenarios: No NSG on a Standard IP
lab.cost: None. The simulation runs entirely in the browser.

troubleshooting.symptom: VM with a Standard public IP is unreachable.
troubleshooting.cause: Standard is closed to inbound by default.
troubleshooting.fix: Add an NSG rule allowing the port.

troubleshooting.symptom: Cannot attach the public IP to a Standard load balancer.
Public IP changed after a deallocation.

comparisons.difference: Outbound-only internet access for a subnet with static public IPs; no inbound.
Static public IPv4 assigned to an instance or NAT gateway.

misconceptions.myth: Public IPs are free when not attached.
misconceptions.reality: Public IPv4 addresses are billed hourly.

misconceptions.myth: A Standard public IP is open to the internet.
misconceptions.reality: Inbound is denied until an NSG allows it.

architectureDecisions: Avoid public IPs on VMs; use Bastion for admin and load balancers or Application Gateway for apps.
Use zone-redundant Standard IPs for production.
Use a prefix for stable allow-listed ranges.

walkthrough.subtitle: Give a resource a public address on the internet, with the right type and settings.
learn: Where public IPs attach, and IP prefixes

steps.label: Reachable
steps.title: A server must be reachable from the internet
body: Customers need a fixed address that does not change, and you want nothing else exposed.

steps.label: SKU
steps.title: Standard public IPs
body: Basic public IPs were retired in September 2025, so new ones are Standard. Standard IPs are static (the address never changes), and can be zone-redundant, zonal or non-zonal. Tier is regional, or global for cross-region load balancers.

steps.label: Secure
steps.title: Closed until you open it
body: A Standard public IP is secure by default: inbound traffic is blocked unless a network security group allows it.

callout.text: VM has a public IP but nobody can connect? Check the NSG on its NIC and subnet.

steps.label: Attach
steps.title: What uses public IPs
body: Attach to a VM's network interface, a load balancer frontend, a NAT gateway, a VPN gateway, Application Gateway, Azure Firewall or Bastion. A public IP prefix reserves a contiguous block of addresses, handy for allow-lists.

steps.label: Recap
steps.title: Public IPs
recap: Static; zone-redundant, zonal or no zone
Secure by default: NSG must allow
Attach to NIC, LB, NAT gateway, gateways, Bastion
Public IP prefix = block of addresses

handsOn.title: Create a static public IP and attach it to a VM
handsOn.cost: Low. One B1s VM costs about US$0.01 per hour. Delete the same day. A Standard public IP adds about US$0.005 per hour.
before: Signed in at portal.azure.com as Owner of a subscription (a free or pay-as-you-go account works). Work in a resource group called rg-az104-lab.
If rg-az104-lab does not exist yet: search 'Resource groups' > Create > name rg-az104-lab, region UAE North (or any region near you) > Review + create > Create.

A virtual network vnet-lab (10.10.0.0/16) in rg-az104-lab with a subnet snet-app (10.10.1.0/24): Virtual networks > + Create > IP addresses tab. For these labs, untick 'Enable private subnet' on snet-app so lab VMs can reach the internet (in production use a NAT gateway instead).

A small Linux VM vm-lab in snet-app of vnet-lab: Virtual machines > + Create. Image Ubuntu 24.04, size Standard_B1s, password authentication, Networking tab: vnet-lab / snet-app, public IP: None, NIC network security group: Basic, public inbound ports: None. If the VM cannot reach the internet later, its subnet is private (the default for new networks): open the virtual network > Subnets, untick 'Enable private subnet', save, then stop and start the VM. In production use a NAT gateway instead.

steps.do: Search 'Public IP addresses' > + Create. Group rg-az104-lab, name pip-lab, region UAE North (or any region near you), SKU Standard, tier Regional, availability zone: Zone-redundant.
steps.see: Assignment is Static (no other choice for Standard).
The IP address, already allocated, and 'Associated to: -'.

steps.do: Open vm-lab > Networking > the network interface > IP configurations > ipconfig1. Associate public IP address: pip-lab. Save.

steps.see: Associated to: the VM's network interface.

steps.do: From Cloud Shell try: curl --max-time 5 http://<the IP>
steps.see: It times out: nothing allows inbound traffic. Standard IPs are closed by default.

steps.do: Dissociate the public IP from the NIC (IP configuration > public IP: Disassociate). Save.
steps.see: The VM has no public IP again.

check: You saw a Standard public IP stay closed until an NSG allows traffic.
cleanup: When you finish for the day: Resource groups > rg-az104-lab > Delete resource group > type the name > Delete. This removes everything inside it.
